analysis.title: Blue Sweep as voters turn their back on Trump
key_insights: Democrats have taken control of both the House and the Senate in the midterms, per news desks. Per AP they hold 52 Senate seats (4 net gain needed) versus 40 Republican with 8 uncalled. In the House Democrats have 194 seats against 218 needed, with 126 uncalled.

SEB expects a slightly more expansionary fiscal policy under a gridlocked Congress, while major spending pushes such as Trump's demand for $1.5 trillion for the Pentagon are blocked. Budget deficits are already on an unsustainable path and neither party is focused on them.

Trump must negotiate with Democrats on budget issues and the 2027 debt ceiling. SEB expects Democrats to seek reversals of health care savings (ACA subsidy extensions, Medicaid work requirements) in exchange for military spending. New government shutdowns are likely regardless of the election result.
Democrats take the Speakership and can bring votes to the floor, but a Trump veto needs a 2/3 majority in both chambers to override. Trump has declared he will be 'Mr Veto'.
Democrats are not historically aggressive on debt ceiling negotiations, but the 2027 debt ceiling gives them leverage.

A Democratic House opens investigations and impeachment procedures against the President and cabinet members. Senate conviction remains unlikely given the 2/3 requirement. Democrats are expected to call CEOs with ties to the administration as witnesses.

A Democratic Senate blocks Trump appointments to the Fed, Supreme Court, cabinet and agencies. Powell can retire without being replaced by a Trump pick, and new attempts to fire Lisa Cook would not open a seat for Trump. Fewer Board members may make the Fed more hawkish because regional Reserve Bank presidents have tended to be more hawkish than the Board.

The President retains room on foreign, immigration and trade policy through executive orders. SEB does not expect the election to stop the war in Iran or further tariffs. Courts, ultimately the Supreme Court, will draw the line.

The lame-duck session is unlikely to produce major Republican legislation. The House majority is slim, many members are leaving, and those who lost seats after Trump endorsed their primary opponents are unlikely to support him. The next Congress is sworn in 3 January 2027.

No major federal change is expected on AI. At state level both parties have distanced themselves from data center expansion. Democratic gubernatorial candidates in Georgia and Texas called for temporary bans on server farm construction, which may force companies to negotiate concessions on energy and water. Democrats have been called winners in both states.

Market reaction: US and European equity futures are lower, with a large decline in Japan. The USD is weaker versus the EUR and US yields are slightly lower. SEB sees the Middle East conflict as the decisive market driver, with mixed White House messaging on escalation versus negotiation.

SEB reads Republican losses as discontent about rising prices and the war with Iran, not necessarily an endorsement of Democratic policies. This matters for 2028 and the balance of power inside the Democratic party and Trump's control of the Republican party.

sector_views.rationale: No major federal change expected on AI. State-level opposition from both parties may force data center builders to make concessions on energy and water supply.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Trump's demand for $1.5 trillion for the Pentagon is unlikely to pass a gridlocked Congress, closing the door to major spending pushes.
SEB expects a modestly looser fiscal stance. This is not bad for bond markets, but deficits are already unsustainable and the shift does not improve them.

risk_factors: Middle East conflict developments, which SEB calls decisive for markets.
Government shutdowns are likely given the need for bipartisan support on annual appropriations.
Unsustainable budget deficit path with neither party focused on it.
State-level restrictions on data center construction.
A possible hawkish tilt at the Fed if the Board has fewer members.
Impeachment and investigation activity against the President and cabinet members.
vol_and_positioning: Equity futures are declining in the US and Europe, with a large decline in Japan. The USD is slightly weaker versus the EUR and US yields are slightly lower.
geopolitical: War in Iran: SEB does not expect the shift in Congress to stop it.
White House sending opposing messages on the Middle East conflict, calling for both escalation and new negotiations.
Tariffs: more tariffs expected from the administration via executive orders, with courts as the limit.
Democratic gubernatorial candidates in Georgia and Texas call for temporary bans on server farm construction.

tension_points.bull_case: A gridlocked Congress leads to slightly more expansionary fiscal policy. SEB says this is not bad for bond markets.
tension_points.bear_case: Budget deficits are already on an unsustainable path and the change is not enough for a sustainable improvement. Neither party is focused on the deficit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 2027 debt ceiling fight or government shutdown could disrupt the outlook, since SEB expects Democrats to use the debt ceiling as leverage.
